Question: Describe your low-code/no-code workflow designer for defining agentic workflows: conditional logic, loops, parallel processing.
Response: Three cooperating layers underpin every workflow and three builder experiences sit on top of them. The execution stack is: (a) Azure Durable Functions as the long-running durable envelope owning phase boundaries, HITL waits at zero compute, checkpoint/replay and geo-replicated state; (b) Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) workflows v1.0 as the per-phase graph of typed executors with conditional routing, fan-out/fan-in, Pregel BSP execution and native pause/resume — wired to DF via Microsoft's productised MAF Durable Task extension for Azure Functions (the "Durable Agent Orchestration" pattern, Feb 2026); (c) GHCP SDK sessions invoked only from MAF agent executor nodes where LLM reasoning is genuinely needed. Most MAF executors are plain Python/C# functions — deterministic by default, agentic by exception. Builder experiences, each producing declarative, Git-committable artefacts flowing through the same APIOps governance pipeline (meeting §6.5 'Low-code artefacts must serialise to the same code/config format as pro-code artefacts'): (1) Pro-code: MAF workflow definitions in Python/.NET (executors, edges, validators) plus GHCP SDK skills in SKILL.md; DF orchestrations invoke MAF workflows as durable activities. Recommended for complex autonomous multi-step workflows. (2) Low-code visual builder — Microsoft Copilot Studio: Microsoft's flagship low-code agent builder with visual drag-and-drop designer, conditional branching, tool bindings (Power Platform connectors + MCP), HITL touchpoints, and knowledge grounding. Copilot Studio agents export as declarative YAML / JSON within Power Platform solutions, Git-committable via Power Platform ALM, versioned through environments (Dev → Test → Prod), and registered with Entra Agent ID (Agent 365 umbrella GA May 2026) — governed by APIM, Purview, and Defender alongside pro-code agents. 60-minute build benchmark hit natively via templates + pre-wired MCP connectors + Foundry IQ knowledge sources, target <30 min. (3) Low-code MCP tools (Azure Logic Apps): visual workflow chaining of 1,400+ connectors (SharePoint, Outlook, Dataverse, SAP, ServiceNow) exposed as MCP tools via APIM's REST→MCP gateway — no-code path for adding tools. Governed identically to hand-written MCP servers. (4) Low-code config (Control Plane UI): skill library (browse/fork/customise), tool catalogue, governance editor, autonomy dials, template fork-and-customise — for operational tuning by process owners, not agent construction; all changes written back to Git via APIOps. (5) 60-minute build benchmark (§6.4): Copilot Studio hits this natively — template + 3 MCP tool connectors + 3 Foundry IQ knowledge sources → publish to Agent 365; end-to-end <30 minutes, scripted for POC evaluation. (6) Agentic builder (design-time): a MAF agent executor generates SKILL.md files from natural-language specifications — typed skill definitions with declared tools, model assignment, governance rules; registered in API Center in Design state; human reviews and approves to promote to Production. Built and demonstrated. (7) Runtime agent assembly: MAF dynamic executor creation + auto-register spawned agents in Entra Agent ID + API Center Design state via governance-gate callback + human promotes to Production. (8) Threadlight (Microsoft delivery accelerator) captures SME interviews into SKILL.md / MAF / MCP artefacts — all Git-inspectable; same API Center governance pathway as hand-written skills.
Key Technologies: GHCP SDK (Python), Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) v1.0 (Python/.NET), MAF Durable Task extension, Azure Durable Functions, Microsoft Copilot Studio (primary low-code visual builder, Power Platform ALM), Azure Logic Apps (low-code MCP), Custom Control Plane UI + template forge (operational config), Threadlight accelerator, Agent 365
POC Demo: POC1: Show a MAF workflow graph per phase (plain-function, agent and validator executors) with parallel invoice processing, orchestrated by a DF envelope with HITL gates. Demonstrate Copilot Studio producing a deployed agent in <30 minutes (60-min build benchmark).

Question: How are agent performance and process status monitored? Describe re-run and terminate capabilities.
Response: Monitoring operates at three levels and spans all three execution layers (DF envelope, MAF workflow graph, GHCP SDK sessions inside agent executors). (1) Fleet Manager agent: continuously reasons about fleet health, SLA risk and anomalies from OTEL telemetry (MAF executor lifecycle spans plus GHCP SDK session spans). Composes the exception-only view for the Control Plane — operators see only workflows needing attention. (2) Foundry Control Plane: platform-level monitoring with agent run rates, error rates, token usage, cost and execution traces. Foundry Evaluators run continuous quality checks. (3) Custom Control Plane UI: operator dashboard with real-time workflow status filterable by agency, market, risk level, jurisdiction, client and workflow type. Re-run: DF supports replaying a workflow from a specific checkpoint; MAF's own checkpoint state is preserved across DF replay via the MAF Durable Task extension, so a phase's graph state resumes exactly where it left off. Terminate: operators can terminate from the Control Plane, which cancels the DF orchestration and triggers compensating actions for any revocable steps already executed.
Key Technologies: Fleet Manager agent, Foundry Control Plane, Custom Control Plane UI, Azure Durable Functions replay/cancel, Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) v1.0, MAF Durable Task extension
POC Demo: POC1: Show workflow terminate from Control Plane with compensating actions. Show re-run of a failed phase from checkpoint.

Question: Describe automatic retry, human notification, graceful fallback, and escalation mechanisms for error handling.
Response: Exception handling is layered across the three execution substrates. (1) MAF agent executor level: the GHCP SDK session inside the executor handles transient errors within its reasoning loop — the model reasons about failures and retries tool calls with adjusted parameters, wrapped by pre/post hooks. Non-revocable actions (external email, offer letter, payment above threshold, ServiceNow JML ticket, A2A outbound, Workday/D365 master data writes, compliance attestation, external publishing) are intercepted at pre-execution and route to approval via the human's PA — execution is deterministic post-approval (no LLM in the send path). High-risk non-revocable actions require dual-control: two distinct Entra identities from two distinct operator groups, enforced by DF orchestration waiting on two distinct raise_event calls. (2) MAF workflow graph level: validator executors between agent executors catch policy or schema violations and route to rejection branches; failed executors can be re-run within MAF's pause/resume lifecycle. (3) Durable Functions level: configurable retry policies with exponential backoff per activity (each MAF workflow invocation is a DF activity via the MAF Durable Task extension). After max retries, the phase enters exception state. (4) Fleet Manager level: detects exceptions across all layers and composes contextual notifications — what happened, what was tried, what it recommends, what the options are. Notifications route to the appropriate human via their PA and preferred surface (Teams, email Adaptive Card, Control Plane). (5) Escalation: if the assigned human does not act within an SLA window, DF timer triggers escalation (zero compute while waiting). (6) Graceful fallback: if a primary integration is unavailable (e.g. Workday API down), the agent executor can fall back to cached data or queue the phase for later retry. If a model endpoint degrades, APIM AI Gateway fails over to an alternative model without an agent restart.
Key Technologies: GHCP SDK error handling, Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) v1.0 validators & pause/resume, MAF Durable Task extension, Azure Durable Functions retry/timer, Fleet Manager exception routing, APIM model failover
POC Demo: POC1: Simulate API timeout on Maconomy — show retry with backoff, fallback, and Fleet Manager notification to Finance BP.

Question: Describe the dashboard for human oversight: role-based views, customisation, visual agent activity monitoring.
Response: The Custom Control Plane UI is a purpose-built React application providing fleet-scale human oversight. Role-based views: Entra RBAC determines what each operator sees — HR BP sees hiring workflows, Finance BP sees budget gates, IT Ops sees provisioning workflows. Each role gets a filtered dashboard with relevant metrics and exception queues. Customisation: operators can configure their view — filter by agency, market, risk level, jurisdiction, client, workflow type. Pin frequently-used filters. Set personal notification preferences. Visual monitoring: real-time workflow status with visual indicators (active, waiting, exception, completed). Fleet health summary from the Fleet Manager. Drill-down from fleet view to individual workflow to specific phase. The Custom Control Plane UI consumes data from Application Insights APIs (traces), Foundry REST APIs (agent inventory), APIM metrics (token/cost), workflow state store (phase status), Fleet Manager assessments (via SignalR real-time), and AG-UI SSE event streams emitted by MAF agent executors (for dynamic per-workflow approval forms, charts, wizards — no hardcoded UI per workflow type). AG-UI mediated by APIM (auth, rate limit, audit) addresses §5.3 RFP 'AG-UI or equivalent: Must support'.
Key Technologies: Custom Control Plane UI (React), SignalR (real-time), AG-UI (SSE dynamic components via APIM), Entra RBAC, Fleet Manager agent
POC Demo: POC1: Live Control Plane dashboard with Finance Controller view managing 30-50 concurrent invoice workflows. Role-filtered views.

Question: How does the platform prioritise and triage items for human intervention? Describe AI-driven prioritisation by criticality, SLA, and confidence.
Response: The Fleet Manager agent provides AI-driven prioritisation. It consumes telemetry from all workflows and reasons about: (1) Business impact — invoice value, candidate seniority, client priority. (2) SLA urgency — how close is the workflow to breaching its SLA deadline. (3) Confidence score — how confident was the agent executor in its recommendation (high confidence items may just need rubber-stamp approval, low confidence items need careful review). (4) Pattern detection — is this exception similar to ones the operator has seen before (surface precedents). The Fleet Manager composes a prioritised exception queue: most urgent/impactful items surface first. Low-risk batches are grouped for bulk approval. The operator sees the Fleet Manager's assessment, not raw telemetry. Agent 365 helps determine routing — who should receive each exception based on role, authority, availability, and timezone.
Key Technologies: Fleet Manager agent (AI-driven prioritisation), Agent 365 (routing), Custom Control Plane UI
POC Demo: POC2: Show prioritised exception queue — compliance flag on German hire ranked above routine scheduling exception based on risk and SLA.

Question: What contextual information is presented to human reviewers? Describe how history, reasoning, and agent context are surfaced for quick decisions.
Response: Instant situational awareness is a primary design goal — full context within 5 seconds of clicking a workflow. The Control Plane drill-down shows: (1) What happened — timeline of phases completed, actions taken, systems touched. (2) What stopped progress — the specific exception or decision point with full context. (3) What the agent tried — reasoning chain from OTEL traces, tool calls attempted, errors encountered. (4) What the agent recommends — the Fleet Manager's recommendation based on policy, precedents, and data. (5) What the options are — approve as-is, modify and approve, reject, escalate, or override. Supporting context: relevant policy excerpts, similar past decisions, cost impact, SLA status. All powered by the Fleet Manager agent's contextual reasoning over OTEL data and the workflow state store. The reasoning chain (OTEL spans) is presented separately from the action ledger so operators can audit the reasoning sequence without viewing prompt bodies (which are redacted by Foundry Guardrails and stored only in Log Analytics, never in App Insights). Structured outputs from agent executors (schema-validated by APIM before propagation) are rendered in the Control Plane alongside the recommendation, with any schema violations surfaced to Fleet Manager. The human's PA can provide additional coaching and knowledge augmentation on demand.
Key Technologies: Fleet Manager agent, OTEL traces, workflow state store, Custom Control Plane UI, PA skill amplification
POC Demo: POC1: Click into an invoice exception — show 5-second situational awareness with full context, recommendation, and options.

Question: How does human feedback loop back into agent improvement? Describe retraining or tuning mechanisms.
Response: Human feedback loops back through three mechanisms. (1) Override logging: when a human overrides an agent executor's recommendation (changes a shortlist, rejects a proposed GL code), the override is logged with full context — the agent executor's recommendation, the human's decision and any reason. (2) Fleet Manager analysis: the Fleet Manager agent analyses override patterns across workflows. If the same type of override repeats, it proposes a skill or threshold adjustment — surfaced on the Control Plane for approval before implementation. (3) Skill crystallisation: proven patterns graduate from an agent executor node to a deterministic plain-function executor in the MAF workflow graph, versioned as a skill in Azure API Center (Design → Preview → Production) and swapped into the graph; the agent executor is preserved as a low-confidence fallback. This is not model fine-tuning (we avoid retraining production models) — it is operational learning where skills, thresholds and graph topology improve based on human expertise, version-controlled and audit-trailed.
Key Technologies: Override logging, Fleet Manager pattern analysis, skill crystallisation via API Center, Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) workflow graph (agent → plain-function executor migration)
POC Demo: POC2: Show override logging and Fleet Manager proposing threshold adjustment after repeated similar overrides.

Question: Describe audit logging and compliance reporting: granularity, immutability, and customisable report generation.
Response: Audit logging is comprehensive and immutable, and spans all three execution layers. Granularity: every DF orchestration event, MAF executor lifecycle event (enter/exit, validator pass/fail), model call, tool call, human interaction, approval decision, policy enforcement event and state change is logged. OTEL spans capture full execution traces (MAF workflow spans are emitted natively; GHCP SDK sessions inside agent executors emit via the SDK TracerProvider). APIM logs all gateway traffic. GHCP SDK hooks log every tool call with workflow context. The action ledger in the workflow state store is append-only and records all actions with revocable/non-revocable classification and the authorising identities — dual-control (two distinct Entra identities from two distinct operator groups) captured for high-risk non-revocable actions. The reasoning chain (OTEL traces from GHCP SDK and MAF) is stored separately from the action ledger with correlated span IDs, so auditors can trace cause and effect without the reasoning chain becoming the audit artefact. Data is classified into 4 classes — Workflow state (Cosmos, CMK), Model context (ephemeral, Guardrails-redacted, never persisted), Audit ledger (Log Analytics, 7-12y immutable), Telemetry (App Insights, no prompt bodies) — each with distinct residency, retention, and redaction rules enforced by APIOps CI gates. Immutability: Azure Log Analytics with archive tier provides 7-12 year retention (immutability enforced via Azure Storage export with immutability policies). Logs are append-only and tamper-evident. Customisable reporting: Log Analytics supports KQL queries; Microsoft Sentinel provides security-focused reporting and automated threat detection. The Custom Control Plane UI can generate compliance reports per workflow, per agent, per jurisdiction.
Key Technologies: Azure Log Analytics (immutable), OTEL tracing (MAF + GHCP SDK), APIM logging, Microsoft Sentinel, action ledger, Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) v1.0
POC Demo: POC1: Generate compliance report for a completed invoice workflow — show full audit trail from receipt to payment.
